quests.instruction: Meera usually leaves her homework until the bus ride to school. What is the most likely consequence?
quests.correctAnswer: Rushed, Messy Work with More Mistakes 📝
options: Extra Time for Play Later 🎮
Better Work Because of the Pressure ⭐
Rushed, Messy Work with More Mistakes 📝
quests.hint: The key is writing on a moving bus with very little time.
quests.explanation: Rushing on a bumpy bus leads to untidy writing and more mistakes. Pressure rarely improves work, and it does not create extra play time.
quests.funFact: Handwriting is harder to control on a moving vehicle, because the paper and the hand move separately.

quests.instruction: Ravi skips drinking water on a hot sports day. What is the most likely consequence?
quests.correctAnswer: Feeling Tired, Dizzy or Headachy 🥵
options: Feeling Tired, Dizzy or Headachy 🥵
Feeling Fresher and Stronger Afterwards 🌿
Running Much Faster Than Usual 🏃
quests.hint: Ask yourself what sweating takes out of the body.
quests.explanation: Sweating removes water, and without replacing it the body can feel tired, dizzy or have a headache. It does not make him faster or fresher.
quests.funFact: Even mild dehydration can make people feel tired and find it harder to concentrate.

quests.instruction: Aman lends his notebook to a friend without writing his name inside. What might happen?
quests.correctAnswer: It Could Get Lost or Mixed Up 📓
options: It Could Get Lost or Mixed Up 📓
It Will Come Back Neater 🧼
The Friend Will Finish It for Him ✍️
quests.hint: Ask yourself how a notebook finds its way home.
quests.explanation: Without a name, a notebook can easily be mixed up with others or lost. It will not tidy itself up, and the friend will not do his work.
quests.funFact: Lost-property boxes at schools are often full of items with no name on them.

quests.instruction: Dev has a free hour. He could play football, or revise for a test tomorrow that he feels unprepared for. What is the most sensible choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Revise for 30 Minutes, Then Play for 30 🔁
options: Revise for the Whole Hour Without a Break 📚
Play Football for the Whole Hour ⚽
Revise for 30 Minutes, Then Play for 30 🔁
quests.hint: Focus on meeting both needs.
quests.explanation: Half an hour of revision helps with the test, and half an hour of play refreshes him. All play or all work leaves out something that matters.
quests.funFact: Exercise raises blood flow to the brain, which can help people feel more alert afterwards.

quests.instruction: Aman can walk to school with a friend by a longer familiar route, or alone by a shorter, quiet shortcut. Which is the better choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Walk with the Friend by the Familiar Route 👫
options: Take Whichever Is Quicker Without Thinking 🏃
Walk Alone by the Quiet Shortcut 🚶
Walk with the Friend by the Familiar Route 👫
quests.hint: Consider safety as well as time.
quests.explanation: Walking with a friend on a familiar route is safer than a quiet shortcut alone. Choosing without thinking ignores the risk.
quests.funFact: Walking in a group makes children easier for drivers and other people to notice.

quests.instruction: Rohan can eat dinner now with the family, or wait and eat later while finishing a video. What is more appropriate?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat with the Family and Watch Afterwards 🍽️
options: Eat with the Family and Watch Afterwards 🍽️
Take the Tablet to the Table with Him 📲
Skip Dinner Altogether to Finish the Video 📱
quests.hint: Consider the people at the table.
quests.explanation: Mealtimes are a chance to be with the family, and the video can wait. Skipping dinner or bringing the tablet to the table takes attention away from them.
quests.funFact: A no-screens rule at the table helps conversation, because everyone's attention is on each other.

quests.instruction: No one is around, and Leo finds the school art cupboard unlocked. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Teacher It Is Unlocked 🔑
options: Take a Few Pens Home in His Bag 🖊️
Tell a Teacher It Is Unlocked 🔑
Leave It Open and Say Nothing 🤐
quests.hint: Work out what keeps school things safe.
quests.explanation: Telling a teacher keeps the supplies safe and shows honesty even when no one is watching. Taking things or ignoring it is not responsible.
quests.funFact: Schools lock supply cupboards so that materials last for everyone.

quests.instruction: Hari's mother has asked him to be in bed by nine, but she is out until ten. What does a responsible child do?
quests.correctAnswer: Go to Bed at Nine as Agreed 🛏️
options: Go to Bed at Nine as Agreed 🛏️
Stay Up Because She Cannot See 🌙
Wait Until Nine Thirty to Be Safe 📺
quests.hint: Focus on keeping an agreement even when no one checks.
quests.explanation: Keeping an agreement when no one is watching shows trust and responsibility. Staying up or bargaining with himself breaks it.
quests.funFact: Handshakes and signed agreements are old ways of showing that a promise will be kept.

quests.instruction: While playing a board game, Aman sees that he could move an extra space without anyone noticing. What is the right choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Play by the Rules 🎲
options: Move the Extra Space Quietly 🤫
Play by the Rules 🎲
Tell the Others After He Wins 🏆
quests.hint: Think about what makes a game fair.
quests.explanation: A game is only fun if everyone follows the same rules. Cheating quietly or confessing after winning spoils it.
quests.funFact: Chess has been played by much the same rules for hundreds of years, which is why people can play it anywhere in the world.

quests.instruction: Mina wants to walk to a friend's house two streets away on her own for the first time. What is the best approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Agree the Route and a Check-in with Her Parents 📞
options: Ask a Stranger to Show Her the Way 🧍
Go Without Telling Anyone Because It Is Close 🏃
Agree the Route and a Check-in with Her Parents 📞
quests.hint: Remember how others can know she is safe.
quests.explanation: Agreeing the route and a check-in lets her try independence safely. Going secretly or asking strangers removes that safety.
quests.funFact: Bicycles often come with stabiliser wheels that are removed once a child is ready.

quests.instruction: Dev wants to cook his own egg. What is a good approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a Grown-up to Supervise the Stove 🍳
options: Ask a Grown-up to Supervise the Stove 🍳
Use the Stove Alone When No One Is Home 🔥
Ask a Grown-up to Start the Stove, Then Leave Him Alone 🍲
quests.hint: Think about learning with support.
quests.explanation: A grown-up nearby lets him learn safely, since stoves can burn. Cooking alone, or being left alone once the stove is lit, raises the risk.
quests.funFact: Learning to cook takes practice, and many people start with simple foods.

quests.instruction: Ila's cough medicine is due at six, but her mother is out. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait or Phone Her Mother for Instructions 📞
options: Ask a Friend's Mum What Dose to Take 💊
Wait or Phone Her Mother for Instructions 📞
Take It from Whichever Bottle Looks Right 🧴
quests.hint: Think about who knows the right amount.
quests.explanation: Medicine must be taken as directed, so she asks her own mother or waits. Advice from another family or guessing at a bottle can be dangerous.
quests.funFact: Medicine labels give the dose because too much can be harmful even when a little helps.

quests.instruction: Rohan wants to practise the drums, but his neighbours have a newborn baby. What is the thoughtful approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Practise at an Agreed Time or Use Practice Pads 🥁
options: Give Up the Drums for Good and Sell the Set 🚫
Practise at an Agreed Time or Use Practice Pads 🥁
Play Louder So the Neighbours Get Used to It 🔊
quests.hint: The key is keeping both his hobby and the baby's sleep.
quests.explanation: Agreeing a time or using quiet practice pads keeps his hobby going and respects the neighbours. Playing louder or giving up are not good compromises.
quests.funFact: Practice pads are rubber surfaces that let drummers practise quietly.

quests.instruction: Anu is cycling along a shared path with walkers. What is the most considerate habit?
quests.correctAnswer: Ring the Bell and Slow Down When Passing 🔔
options: Ride Fast and Close to the People Walking 🚴
Stop in the Middle of the Path to Chat 🛑
Ring the Bell and Slow Down When Passing 🔔
quests.hint: Decide how people on foot can hear you coming.
quests.explanation: A bell warns people, and slowing down gives them space. Riding fast near people or stopping in the path puts them at risk.
quests.funFact: Shared paths often have a painted line or a sign showing which side is for cyclists.

quests.instruction: Hari's group project partner is not doing their share. What is the most mature response?
quests.correctAnswer: Talk Calmly, Then Ask the Teacher if Needed 🗣️
options: Refuse to Work with the Group Ever Again 🚫
Talk Calmly, Then Ask the Teacher if Needed 🗣️
Do Everything Alone and Complain About It Later 😤
quests.hint: The key is solving the problem with the person first.
quests.explanation: Talking calmly gives the partner a chance to change, and the teacher can help if needed. Doing everything or refusing to work together does not solve it.
quests.funFact: Ants and bees share work in a colony, with each one doing a task for the group.

quests.instruction: A classmate calls out a wrong answer, and Aman knows it is wrong. What is the most appropriate response?
quests.correctAnswer: Stay Kind and Let the Teacher Help 🙂
options: Laugh Loudly 😆
Stay Kind and Let the Teacher Help 🙂
Shout the Right Answer to Embarrass Him 📢
quests.hint: Ask yourself how it feels to be wrong in front of others.
quests.explanation: Staying kind lets the teacher correct the answer without hurting feelings. Laughing or shouting would embarrass the classmate.
quests.funFact: Scientists treat mistakes as useful, because experiments that go wrong teach them something.

quests.instruction: A friend is using a method for a sum that Dev thinks is wrong. What is the most helpful thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask to Compare Methods Together 🤝
options: Ask to Compare Methods Together 🤝
Tell Her She Is Wrong and Walk Off 🙄
Copy Her Without Checking 📝
quests.hint: Focus on finding out who is right.
quests.explanation: Comparing methods lets both check the answer and learn. Walking off or copying without checking does not help.
quests.funFact: There are often several correct ways to reach the same answer in maths.

quests.instruction: A younger child forgets the rules of a game halfway through. What is the best response?
quests.correctAnswer: Remind Them Gently and Patiently 🙂
options: Take Over and Play the Game for Them 😠
Tell Everyone They Are Slow 🐌
Remind Them Gently and Patiently 🙂
quests.hint: The clue is how you want to be treated when you are learning.
quests.explanation: A gentle reminder helps the child learn and keeps the game friendly. Taking over or mocking them does not.
quests.funFact: Reading aloud to a younger child helps both of them: the listener learns words and the reader practises fluency.

quests.instruction: Aman has homework to finish and a friend is calling, when his mother asks him to take a parcel to a neighbour who is waiting for it. What should he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Do the Errand Now, Then the Rest 📦
options: Finish Everything Else First 🕰️
Ask His Sister to Do It Without Telling Her 🙄
Do the Errand Now, Then the Rest 📦
quests.hint: Consider who is waiting.
quests.explanation: Someone is waiting for the parcel, so it is the time-sensitive job. Homework and the call can wait a short time.
quests.funFact: Emergency rooms use triage, which means treating the most urgent patients first.

quests.instruction: Zoya has a piano exam in a week, and a friend's party is the evening before. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Practise Earlier, Then Go for a Short While 🎹
options: Practise Earlier, Then Go for a Short While 🎹
Stay at the Party Late and Skip Practice 🎉
Skip the Exam to Enjoy the Party 🚫
quests.hint: Remember how to keep both without risking the exam.
quests.explanation: Practising earlier and going for a short time lets her enjoy the party and still be rested for the exam. Skipping either or staying late is worse.
quests.funFact: Rested hands and a clear mind help performers do their best.

quests.instruction: Ila has two deadlines on Friday. One piece of work is worth far more marks. She has two days. How should she use the time?
quests.correctAnswer: Spend More Time on the Bigger One 📝
options: Spend More Time on the Bigger One 📝
Do Only the Easier One 🧩
Split the Time Equally Without Thinking 🎲
quests.hint: Think about where time is most valuable.
quests.explanation: More marks mean more value, so more time goes there, while the smaller task still gets done. Ignoring one or splitting time without thinking is less wise.
quests.funFact: Students often use a planner or diary to record deadlines.

quests.instruction: On a school trip, Leo sees some litter in a quiet park as the class is about to leave. What might he do?
quests.correctAnswer: Pick Up What Is Safe and Put It in a Bin 🗑️
options: Add His Own Wrapper Because It Is Already Messy 🤷
Pick Up What Is Safe and Put It in a Bin 🗑️
Leave It for Someone Else 🚶
quests.hint: Think about leaving a place better than you found it.
quests.explanation: Picking up safe litter and binning it helps keep the park clean. Leaving it or adding more makes it worse. He should avoid sharp or dirty items.
quests.funFact: Millions of volunteers take part in World Cleanup Day to pick up litter.

quests.instruction: Anu notices a tap dripping in the school toilets. What should she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a Teacher or Caretaker 🚰
options: Twist It Harder with All Her Strength 💪
Tell a Teacher or Caretaker 🚰
Ignore It Because Someone Will See 🙈
quests.hint: Consider who can fix it.
quests.explanation: A teacher or caretaker can arrange a repair. Ignoring it wastes water, and forcing the tap could break it.
quests.funFact: A dripping tap can waste thousands of litres of water in a year.

quests.instruction: The class garden needs watering during a long holiday. What is the responsible plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Make a Rota So Different Families Take Turns 🪴
options: Make a Rota So Different Families Take Turns 🪴
Water It All at Once Just Before Leaving 🚿
Hope the Monsoon Rain Will Do All the Work 🌧️
quests.hint: Think about regular care while no one is at school.
quests.explanation: A rota shares the work and keeps the plants watered regularly. Hoping for rain or one big watering before leaving is not enough.
quests.funFact: Community gardens often use rotas so that many people share the care.

quests.instruction: Friends dare Mina to jump from a high wall. What is the best response?
quests.correctAnswer: Say No and Suggest a Safer Game 🙅
options: Jump Quickly to Show She Is Brave 🧗
Jump Slowly Just the Once to Try 🐢
Say No and Suggest a Safer Game 🙅
quests.hint: Focus on being brave in a way that does not risk injury.
quests.explanation: Saying no and suggesting something else is a confident, safe choice. Jumping, even slowly, risks serious injury.
quests.funFact: Suggesting a different game gives friends a way to change plans without anyone losing face.

quests.instruction: Dia's friends are still chatting online past her agreed limit. What helps her stick to the limit?
quests.correctAnswer: Say She Will Chat Tomorrow and Log Off 📴
options: Say She Will Chat Tomorrow and Log Off 📴
Stay Online Until Everybody Else Leaves 💬
Hide the Time on the Clock Face 🕰️
quests.hint: Think about keeping an agreement without losing friends.
quests.explanation: Saying she will chat tomorrow keeps the agreement and the friendship. Staying or hiding the clock breaks the limit.
quests.funFact: Apps and phones can show how long you have spent on screens each day.

quests.instruction: Aman wants to try a new sport but feels nervous. What is a healthy approach?
quests.correctAnswer: Try a Beginner Session with a Coach 🏏
options: Refuse Because He Might Fail 🏳️
Join an Advanced Match Straight Away 🔥
Try a Beginner Session with a Coach 🏏
quests.hint: Think about starting at the right level.
quests.explanation: A beginner session lets him learn safely and build confidence. Refusing misses the chance, and an advanced match is too much too soon.
quests.funFact: Most clubs offer beginner sessions where everyone starts from the same point.

quests.instruction: Which choice best shows responsibility?
quests.correctAnswer: Doing the Job Well When No One Is Watching 👀
options: Doing It Only When Someone Else Is Checking Up 🔍
Doing It Only When There Is a Reward 🏅
Doing the Job Well When No One Is Watching 👀
quests.hint: The clue is what you do when no one will know.
quests.explanation: Responsibility means doing the right thing because it matters, whether or not anyone is watching or rewarding. Rewards or checks only motivate for a while.
quests.funFact: The word 'responsible' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to answer' for something.

quests.instruction: How can you decide between two good activities when you cannot do both?
quests.correctAnswer: Weigh Deadlines, Safety and Who Needs You ⚖️
options: Pick Whatever Your Closest Friend Chooses 👫
Weigh Deadlines, Safety and Who Needs You ⚖️
Pick the One That Is Quickest to Do 🏃
quests.hint: Decide what matters most.
quests.explanation: Deadlines, safety and the people relying on you show which choice matters most. Speed or copying a friend does not.
quests.funFact: Pilots are trained to fly the plane first in an emergency, then navigate, then communicate.

quests.instruction: Which statement shows good independence?
quests.correctAnswer: Doing Things Myself and Asking When Unsure 🙋
options: Waiting for Someone to Do Everything for Me 🕰️
Doing Things Myself and Asking When Unsure 🙋
Never Asking for Help, Even in Danger 🚫
quests.hint: The key is the difference between independent and alone.
quests.explanation: Independence means doing what you can and asking when you are unsure. Never asking can be dangerous, and waiting for help means no independence.
quests.funFact: Even astronauts rely on mission control for help, which shows that asking for support is part of being capable.
